newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S., S.Korea kick off military, civil exercises.
newsitem.headline: U.S., S.Korea kick off military, civil exercises.

text.p: The United States and South Korea on Monday launched joint military exercises to test their preparedness against threats from North Korea, a Seoul defence ministry spokesman said.

South Korea's Defence Minister Kim Dong-jin called a simulated emergency meeting of military commanders while ministry officials prepared for an urgent security consultation meeting with the United States, he said.

The annual manoeuvres, codenamed Ulchi Focus Lens, would feature computer-simulated war games and involve tens of thousands of South Korean troops as well as 16,500 U.S. soldiers, military officials said.
A defence ministry statement said this year's exercise was upgraded to include "situation drills aimed at improving capability in a real crisis".
"The danger of reckless provocation has increased because of growing uncertainty caused by North Korea's food crisis," it said.
In parallel with the war games, due to last until August 29, South Korea is holding a government-level command post exercise and air-raid drills involving citizens.
Experts have warned of a possible collapse of impoverished North Korea which has been hit hard by famine and an acute energy shortage.
To make the exercises more real, 28 fighter jets, posing as enemy planes, will appear unannounced over 40 South Korean cities, a military spokesman said.

"Ulchi Focus Lens is designed to evaluate and improve combined and joint coordination, procedures, plans and systems necessary for the conduct of contingency operations of the Republic of Korea and the U.S. government in the defence of the Republic of Korea," a U.S. military spokesman said.
Seoul officials said the exercises had long been planned and had nothing to do with four-nation peace talks being arranged by the two Koreas, the United States and China.

Senior officials of the four countries failed to set an agenda in a New York meeting earlier this month but they agreed to try again on September 15 to arrange substantive negotiations for peace on the Korean peninsula.

The four-nation talks are designed to work out tension-reducing steps and a peace treaty to replace the armistice that ended fighting, but not technically the war itself, in the 1950-53 Korean conflict.
North Korea has criticised the United States and South Korea for planning Ulchi Focus Lens, describing the exercise "an extremely threatening act".

"They (the U.S. and South Korea) are talking peace but if they are going to act against the process with these war drills, then there is no reason for communication and the talks have no meaning," a North Korean spokesman said earlier this month.
Seoul and Washington have carried out joint military exercises every year since 1976.
In March they cancelled larger military exercises, Team Spirit, in a goodwill gesture to coax North Korea towards the four-party peace talks.
Team Spirit, which used to be held annually, has been a major source of inter-Korean friction, with the North calling it preparation for an invasion. The manoeuvres were last held in 1993.
About 655,000 South Korean troops, backed by 37,000 U.S. servicemen, confront North Korea's 1.1 million-strong army across the world's last Cold War frontier.
